title: Wire the exclusive store lock into the broker session, watch and process entry
description:
Build-order link 4 of 4 — the row that makes "locked launch" TRUE. Carved by architect-d950bd95 on 2026-08-26 at HEAD 1214c5b3 from the human handoff on task-a341bfb6. Links 1-3: task-3e3ca3b4 (wire vocabulary), task-913bce17 (opcode 3), order 1.468 (store-lock authority).

WHY THIS ROW EXISTS. After links 1-3 the broker can DECODE opcode 3, carry a store path, and NAME a store-lock refusal — but nothing acquires a lock during a launch. A "locked project launch" that takes no lock is a silent exclusivity hole, and the epic's rail 4 forbids leaving a P1 boundary mock-proven. Until this row lands, task-a341bfb6's consumer and its parent task-76d502d7 must not claim the store is exclusively owned.

MEASURED, do not re-derive. Dirty WIP already carries the wiring: session.rs gains `run_with_store_lock<B,S,L>` and `refuse_store_lock`; session_accept.rs is UNTRACKED at 41 lines and pulls accept handling out of session.rs (it imports control::{AcceptState, Accepted, LaunchRequest}, frames, protocol, refusal::Refused and session::{note, refuse_protocol, Wiring}); watch.rs has a 21-line diff; main.rs swaps LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_MS for PROVIDER_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_MS, constructs SystemStoreLocks, calls run_with_store_lock and drops the guard AFTER descriptor teardown; tests/session.rs gains 131 lines including a scripted authority whose Drop logs "drop-store-lock".

ORDERING IS A SAFETY CONSTRAINT, not paperwork: the guard must be acquired BEFORE any Job or process is created and released AFTER final descriptor teardown. Acquiring late opens a window where two hosts both own the store; releasing early opens one where a second host starts while the first is still tearing down.

EXCLUDED. windows-broker-path.ts and its untracked test (broker resolution for packed artifacts) are a separate concern and stay dirty.

An opcode-3 launch whose store is already held refuses at the store-lock layer WITHOUT creating a host: the ordered call log contains acquire and contains NO Job or process creation entry, and the emitted frame decodes to RefusalLayer::StoreLock with StoreLockReason::Contended's ordinal and the numeric Windows code. Assert the refusing layer AND the reason ordinal, not merely that the launch failed.

A project-stack launch has NO provider deadline but still polls control every slice, while an ordinary opcode-1 launch keeps PROVIDER_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_MS: assert both arms, so the timeout split cannot silently collapse into one behaviour. Ordinary launches take no store lock at all — assert the call log has no acquire entry for opcode 1.

Each drill must red the arm that names it and no other, proving neither ordering property is being certified by a downstream fence.
